title: Fixed-Node Quadrature for the Shape Likelihood

# Fixed-Node Quadrature for the Shape Likelihood

::: {.callout-note}
This page documents [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorFixedQuad]]: the same
exact marginalization integral as [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorQuad]], but
evaluated with fixed node counts instead of adaptive Divonne cubature. See
`docs/theory/wl_shape_factor_history.md` for the design history behind this
class.
:::

## Two fixed quadrature schemes, chosen per galaxy

$$
P(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} \mid g) = \int_{|\chi_I|<1} \mathrm{d}^2\chi_I\,
P_\mathrm{pop}(\chi_I)\, N_2\big(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} - f_g(\chi_I);\,
\sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2\big)
$$

is evaluated via one of two schemes, picked from
$(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs},\sigma_\mathrm{noise})$ alone --- never $g$:

- Two-panel $\psi$, for a localized noise kernel (most galaxies).
- Native $\chi_I$-polar, for a broad noise kernel --- specifically when the
  entire unit disc lies within $N_\sigma\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ of
  $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$:
  $$1+|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}| \le N_\sigma\,\sigma_\mathrm{noise},
  \qquad N_\sigma=8.$$
  ($1+|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|$ is the distance from $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$
  to the farthest point of the unit disc, so this condition holds exactly
  when the noise kernel already covers the whole disc.)

Both schemes are exact: no truncation or linearization is applied. They were
validated against an independent scipy integral across population shape,
$|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|$, $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$, $g$ and both ellipticity
conventions, giving a 2.0% worst case and $\sim10^{-6}$ median error.

## Two-panel $\psi$

Same $\psi$-reparametrization [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorQuad]] uses:
$\chi_L=f_h(\psi)$, $h$ the shear with $f_h(0)=\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$
exactly, so $\psi=0$ always maps to the noise kernel's own peak. $\psi$ is
integrated in its own polar coordinates $(\rho,\theta)$, with $\rho$ split
into two independent Gauss--Legendre panels, $[0,R_\sigma)$ and
$[R_\sigma,1)$ (`n-radial` nodes each), concentrating resolution where the
noise kernel's mass actually is. $\theta$ is equally spaced (`n-angular`
nodes) and offset by $\phi=\arg\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ so a coarse grid stays
rotation-covariant.

### $R_\sigma$: the split radius

$R_\sigma$ is the radius of the $\psi$-preimage of the physical noise disc
$\{\chi_L:|\chi_L-\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}|\le N_\sigma\sigma_\mathrm{noise}\}$,
computed exactly (Möbius maps send circles to circles) from three boundary
points mapped through $f_h^{-1}$ and circumscribed:
$$
R_\sigma = \min\!\big(0.98,\ |c|+r\big),
$$
$c,r$ the center/radius of the circle through
$f_h^{-1}(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}+N_\sigma\sigma_\mathrm{noise}e^{i\theta_k})$
at $\theta_k=0,\tfrac{2\pi}{3},\tfrac{4\pi}{3}$.

### Puncture correction

The integrand only ever evaluates the bracket
$N_2(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}-\chi_L)-N_0$, $N_0=N_2(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}-\chi_{L0})$,
$\chi_{L0}=f_g(0)$, with $N_0$ added back once after the sum via
$\int P_\mathrm{pop}=1$. This keeps the summed integrand finite everywhere,
including for a [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapePopBeta]] population with
$\alpha<2$, whose area density $P_\mathrm{pop}(r)/(2\pi r)$ diverges at
$r=0$ --- every domain node has some $g$ where the implied
$\chi_I(g,\chi_L)$ is exactly $0$.

## Native $\chi_I$-polar

Integrates directly in $\chi_I$'s own polar coordinates, with fixed nodes
$\chi_I=\rho\,e^{i\theta}$ ($\rho$: Gauss--Legendre on $[0,1)$; $\theta$:
equally spaced, same $\phi$ offset as above). Because this grid is centered
on $\chi_I=0$ itself:

- No Jacobian for the population term. The quadrature measure's own
  $\rho\,\mathrm{d}\rho$ cancels $P_\mathrm{pop}(\rho)/(2\pi\rho)$'s
  $1/\rho$ analytically --- the per-node weight is just
  $w_\rho w_\theta/(2\pi)$ times $P_\mathrm{pop}(\rho)$ directly.
- No puncture correction. The noise kernel
  $N_2(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}-f_g(\chi_I))$ is evaluated plainly --- a bounded
  exponential, with no singular point in this domain to protect against.

## `use-marginal-spline`: caching the marginal as a function of $g$

Both branches share the same per-galaxy domain cache (`n-radial`/`n-angular`
sized nodes, rebuilt only when $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$/$\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$
change, never $g$) and the same opt-in `use-marginal-spline` mechanism:
$\ln P(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}\mid g)$ cached as a bivariate function of $g$
over $[-g_\mathrm{max},g_\mathrm{max}]^2$ (`spline-g-max`), built lazily via
this codebase's autoknots 2D spline machinery for populations whose area
density stays bounded at $r=0$, or a plain fixed-knot grid (never adaptive)
for populations that diverge there.

## {#sec-limits} Limitation: narrow populations

A fixed grid cannot resolve a population much narrower than its node
spacing, in either branch. Production only uses a Gaussian population with
$\sigma_\mathrm{pop}\in(0.2,0.4)$, comfortably inside the validated regime;
use `Quad` for narrower or more exotic populations.

## `n-radial`/`n-angular`

Both properties are `CONSTRUCT_ONLY` and size whichever grid is chosen:
`n-radial` nodes per panel for two-panel (so $2\times$`n-radial` radial
nodes total), or `n-radial` nodes in the one grid for native $\chi_I$.
Default 15 for both.

See `tests/python/nc/lss/galaxy/test_galaxy_shape_factor_fixed_quad.py` for
the test suite, including `nc_galaxy_shape_factor_fixed_quad_eval_two_panel()`/
`_eval_chi_i_native()`, test-only accessors that force one branch regardless
of the switch.
